stem: Meena's teacher asks the class to group objects by a common property. Which statement about grouping objects is not correct?

options.text: A steel spoon, a steel plate and an iron nail can be grouped together because they are all made of metal.
Grouping objects always means putting any objects together, even when no common property is used.
A red ball, a red pencil and a red eraser can be grouped together because they share the same colour.
A cotton shirt, a woollen cap and a silk scarf can be grouped together because they are all made of fabric.

teacher.key_rationale: Classification requires grouping by a named common property (material, colour, etc.). Options A, C and D each correctly name a shared property; only B claims grouping needs no common property, which is the incorrect statement, so B is the key.
